source_text: Et quod usque ad legem est, ostenditur non esse post legem, ostenditur postremo non esse post Christum.
pass_a_gloss: And what is until the law is shown not to be after the law, is shown finally not to be after Christ.
pass_b_english: And what exists until the law is shown not to exist after the law—shown, at any rate, not to exist after Christ (compare Romans 5:13) (Romans 5:13).

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
